claims.natural_statement: For every r>=1 there are C_r>0 and d_r>=r such that for every d>=d_r, every faithful normal tracial von Neumann algebra, every r unital scalar-free copies of M_d, and every multiset W of r labels, ||B_W|| <= 7 sqrt((r-1)!) d^(-(r-1)/2) for distinct labels and <= C_r d^(-(r-1)/2) otherwise (lem:free-words).

For every N>=1 there exists d_0(N) such that for every d>=d_0(N), all 1<=r<=N and every fixed label a, the sum of beta_W^2 over r-element multisets W containing a, counted once, is <=64, with beta_W as in lem:free-words (cor:through-label).

Every centered free word in distinct copy positions is exactly the sum of r+1 annihilation/creation cuts and r single-preservation cuts on the full reduced free-product Hilbert space, with the label-independent domain restrictions E_p and E in the manuscript; each cut norm is bounded by d^(-(p+q)/2) times its label-tuple matrix norm, for arbitrary Hilbert-space tails.

For any r-element set W and any cut, the no-preservation tuple matrix has norm sqrt(p!q!), p+q=r. For a preservation cut p+q=r-1, the uncompressed missing-label projection matrix is a contraction and the tuple-matrix norm is <=sqrt(p!q!)(1+sqrt((p+1)(q+1))/d). There is no additional permutation multiplicity.

For every m>=0, sum_(p=0)^m binom(m,p)^(-1/2)<=5. Scalar restoration contributes at most r! H_r d^(-r/2), H_r=1+sum_(l=1)^(r-1)binom(r,l)(2l+1). For r>=2, the number of repeated-label r-multisets containing a is at most A_r d^(r-2), A_r=sum_(u=0)^(r-2)binom(r-1,u)/u!.

For every epsilon>0 a universal delta>0 makes any two unital von Neumann algebras on any complex Hilbert space at KK distance below delta conjugate by a unitary u with ||u-I||<epsilon (Universal manuscript thm:main).
An absolute C_amp bounds ||ad_h|M||_cb by C_amp ||ad_h|M|| for every separably acting II_1 factor, every representation and selfadjoint h (thm:amplification).
For every unital represented Cstar algebra A and h, ||([h,a_i])||_col <=8 ||ad_h|A|| ||(a_i)||_col (lem:column-commutator).
For every matrix level n, P=M_n(M) has an ultrapower Haar unitary scalar-free from P with full-matrix unitary lifts s_j satisfying ||[I_n tensor h,s_j]||<=2||ad_h|M|| (lem:free-lifts).

The controlled lifts, clipping and scalar recovery arguments after cor:through-label imply the claimed positive scalar weak limit detecting all matrix commutators; this downstream burden is not settled by the present mission.

The boundary correction, intertwiner and diagonal-unitary implications lem:boundary-correction, lem:boundary-intertwiner and lem:boundary-diagonal-unitary hold with their stated uniform bounds (Section 04).
The finite-factor uniform stability theorem thm:finite follows with uniform constants as stated in Section 05.

Prepared-pair, modular-graph/cut and modular-alignment implications (prop:prepared-pair, prop:modular-graphs, cor:modular-cuts, prop:modular-alignment) and normalizer correction in Sections 06-07 are valid.
Core descent prop:core-descent and the uniform separably acting factor theorem thm:factors hold as stated in Section 08.
Center matching, fiber-gap, measurable implementers, separable tests and thm:separable-algebras in Section 09 extend the factor theorem to the full arbitrary-cardinality main theorem.

There are common-identity von Neumann pairs M_n,N_n on separable H_n with one-sided gap gamma(M_n,N_n)->0, but a fixed epsilon_0>0 lower-bounds ||u-I|| for every spatial embedding u M_n u* subset N_n for all sufficiently large n (Near-Inclusions thm:main).
The uniform Fourier circle construction prop:circle and near-inclusion estimate prop:near convert a vanishing unitary commutator into vanishing one-sided gap.
The clock/shift obstruction lem:clock and corner recovery lem:corner rule out small spatial embeddings despite the small commutator.

For every epsilon>0 there exist common-identity norm-separable Cstar algebras A,B on a separable H with KK(A,B)<epsilon and A''=B'', but no unitary spatially conjugates A and B (Cstar manuscript thm:main).
The sequence-space invariant prop:sequences/lem:invariant/cor:obstruction and the tree deformation lem:tree give the claimed nonconjugacy obstruction.

Absorption, ambient representation, good/bad inclusions and free-norm comparison (lem:absorption, lem:ambient, lem:good-inclusion, lem:free-norm, lem:bad-inclusion) supply the closeness and common bicommutant of the Cstar construction.

All-multiset strengthening: for scalar-free equal-trace orthogonal projection partitions (no full matrix structure required), every r>=1 and every multiset W, ||B_W||<=5 sqrt((r-1)!) d^(-(r-1)/2) whenever d>=D_r=max(8r,4r r! (H_r+r+1)^2), H_r=1+(r+1)(2^r-2). With this common beta, the through-label squared sum is <=26 whenever also d>=13(r-1)(r-2); one finite maximum threshold works for every r<=N.

For arbitrary finite alphabets and multiset W, A+B+{a}=W determines A from (B,a), B from (A,a), and a from (A,B). Consequently a finite missing-label edge set has injective projections onto (A,a) and (B,a), and its nonnegative input-label energy sum is at most the sum over all available input-label coordinates. The real all-ones m-by-n matrix has squared energy bound mn and attains that coefficient on constant vectors. The scalar Cauchy and product induction identities used for the uniform estimates hold for all parameters.

Every centered free word in distinct copy positions is exactly the sum of r+1 annihilation/creation cuts and r single-preservation cuts on the full reduced free-product Hilbert space, with the label-independent domain restrictions E_p and E in the manuscript; each cut norm is bounded by d^(-(p+q)/2) times its label-tuple matrix norm, for arbitrary Hilbert-space tails.

claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

namespace FreeWordAudit

variable {α : Type*}

theorem missing_left_unique {A A' B W : Multiset α} {a : α}
    (h : A + B + {a} = W) (h' : A' + B + {a} = W) : A = A' := by
  exact add_right_cancel (add_right_cancel (h.trans h'.symm))

theorem missing_right_unique {A B B' W : Multiset α} {a : α}
    (h : A + B + {a} = W) (h' : A + B' + {a} = W) : B = B' := by
  exact add_left_cancel (add_right_cancel (h.trans h'.symm))

theorem missing_label_unique {A B W : Multiset α} {a b : α}
    (h : A + B + {a} = W) (h' : A + B + {b} = W) : a = b := by
  have hs : ({a} : Multiset α) = {b} := add_left_cancel (h.trans h'.symm)
  simpa using hs

theorem missing_energy_le [DecidableEq α]
    (W : Multiset α)
    (s : Finset (Multiset α × (Multiset α × α)))
    (I : Finset (Multiset α × α))
    (hs : ∀ e ∈ s, e.1 + e.2.1 + {e.2.2} = W)
    (hI : ∀ e ∈ s, e.2 ∈ I)
    (w : (Multiset α × α) → ℝ)
    (hw : ∀ i ∈ I, 0 ≤ w i) :
    (∑ e ∈ s, w e.2) ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, w i := by
  classical
  have hinj : Set.InjOn
      (fun e : Multiset α × (Multiset α × α) => e.2) s := by
    intro e he f hf h
    have hB : e.2.1 = f.2.1 := congrArg Prod.fst h
    have ha : e.2.2 = f.2.2 := congrArg Prod.snd h
    have hfe : f.1 + e.2.1 + {e.2.2} = W := by
      simpa only [hB, ha] using hs f hf
    exact Prod.ext (missing_left_unique (hs e he) hfe) h
  calc
    (∑ e ∈ s, w e.2) =
        ∑ i ∈ s.image (fun e => e.2), w i := by
      symm
      exact Finset.sum_image hinj
    _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, w i := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
      · intro i hi
        obtain ⟨e, he, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
        exact hI e he
      · intro i hi _
        exact hw i hi

theorem all_ones_energy_bound (m n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
    (m : ℝ) * (∑ j, x j) ^ 2 ≤
      (m : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) * (∑ j, (x j) ^ 2) := by
  have h := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq
    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) x (fun _ => (1 : ℝ))
  have hc : (∑ j, x j) ^ 2 ≤ (n : ℝ) * (∑ j, (x j) ^ 2) := by
    simpa [mul_comm] using h
  calc
    (m : ℝ) * (∑ j, x j) ^ 2 ≤
        (m : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) * (∑ j, (x j) ^ 2)) :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hc (Nat.cast_nonneg m)
    _ = _ := by ring

theorem all_ones_constant_attains (m n : ℕ) (c : ℝ) :
    (m : ℝ) * (∑ _j : Fin n, c) ^ 2 =
      (m : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) * (∑ _j : Fin n, c ^ 2) := by
  simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
  ring

theorem middle_tail_algebra (m : ℝ) (hm : 5 ≤ m) :
    (m - 3) ^ 2 ≤ (m - 1) * (m - 4) := by
  nlinarith

theorem weighted_cauchy_identity (u v : ℝ) :
    3 * (u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 / 2) - (u + v) ^ 2 =
      (2 * u - v) ^ 2 / 2 := by
  ring

theorem scalar_tail_lt_two (u v : ℝ)
    (h : u ^ 2 + v ^ 2 / 2 ≤ 1) : u + v < 2 := by
  have hs := sq_nonneg (2 * u - v)
  have ht := sq_nonneg (u + v - 2)
  nlinarith

theorem product_step (s x : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    (1 + x) * (1 - s - x) ≤ 1 - s := by
  nlinarith [mul_nonneg hs hx, sq_nonneg x]

theorem product_defect_bound {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → ℝ) :
    (∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ x i) →
      (∏ i ∈ s, (1 + x i)) * (1 - ∑ i ∈ s, x i) ≤ 1 := by
  classical
  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
  | empty => simp
  | @insert a s ha ih =>
      intro hx
      have hxa : 0 ≤ x a := hx a (by simp)
      have hxs : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ x i := by
        intro i hi
        exact hx i (by simp [hi])
      have hsum : 0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, x i := Finset.sum_nonneg hxs
      have hprod : 0 ≤ ∏ i ∈ s, (1 + x i) :=
        Finset.prod_nonneg (by
          intro i hi
          linarith [hxs i hi])
      have hstep := product_step (∑ i ∈ s, x i) (x a) hsum hxa
      rw [Finset.prod_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha]
      calc
        (1 + x a) * (∏ i ∈ s, (1 + x i)) *
            (1 - (x a + ∑ i ∈ s, x i)) =
            (∏ i ∈ s, (1 + x i)) *
              ((1 + x a) * (1 - (∑ i ∈ s, x i) - x a)) := by ring
        _ ≤ (∏ i ∈ s, (1 + x i)) * (1 - ∑ i ∈ s, x i) :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hstep hprod
        _ ≤ 1 := ih hxs

theorem through_twenty_six (P s : ℝ) (hP : 0 ≤ P)
    (hs : s ≤ 1 / 26) (h : P * (1 - s) ≤ 1) : 25 * P ≤ 26 := by
  have hm : 0 ≤ P * (1 / 26 - s) := mul_nonneg hP (by linarith)
  nlinarith

end FreeWordAudit

retired_assumptions.reason: report.md Section 1 independently proves the reduced-word inner products, faithful norm model, exact component actions, copy-index source restrictions, finite cut identity and all-tail bounded extension; Fact 2.6 is now prior context only, not an external premise.
